subproblem.title: First and second derivatives of z ↦ h(x − s z) for an arbitrary h
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let h : ℝⁿ → ℝ (= Euclid n → ℝ) be an arbitrary function (no regularity assumed), let x ∈ ℝⁿ and s ∈ ℝ, and put G(z) := h(x − s z). Then for all y, a, b ∈ ℝⁿ: DG(y)a = −(s·Dh(x − s y)a) and D²G(y)(a, b) = s²·D²h(x − s y)(a, b). Here D = fderiv ℝ and D²F(y)(a, b) = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 F y ![a, b] are Mathlib's total derivatives, which are 0 at points of non-differentiability.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (x : Euclid n) (s : ℝ) (y a b : Euclid n), fderiv ℝ (fun z : Euclid n => h (x - s • z)) y a = -(s * fderiv ℝ h (x - s • y) a) ∧ iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 (fun z : Euclid n => h (x - s • z)) y ![a, b] = s ^ 2 * iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h (x - s • y) ![a, b]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4, first bullet, of the parent proof: DG(y) = −s·Dh(x − s y) and D²G(y)(a, b) = s²·D²h(x − s y)(a, b). Here it is proved for an arbitrary function h and every y. The identities hold even where h is not differentiable, because z ↦ x − s z is an affine isomorphism when s ≠ 0 and constant when s = 0.

1. (Case s = 0.) Then G(z) = h(x) for all z, so G is constant. Hence DG(y) = 0, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 G y = 0 (iteratedFDeriv_const_of_ne, since 2 ≠ 0). The right-hand sides are −(0·Dh(x)a) = 0 and 0²·D²h(x)(a, b) = 0. Both identities hold.

2. (Case s ≠ 0: factorisation.) Let L : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, L(z) := (−s)z. Since −s ≠ 0, L is a continuous linear equivalence (ContinuousLinearEquiv.smulLeft of the unit −s, with inverse z ↦ (−s)⁻¹z). Let T(w) := h(x + w). Then G = T ∘ L, because x − s z = x + (−s)z.

3. (Composition with an isomorphism needs no differentiability.)
- For any function F and continuous linear equivalence L, F ∘ L is differentiable at y iff F is differentiable at L(y), since F = (F ∘ L) ∘ L⁻¹. If so, D(F ∘ L)(y) = DF(L y) ∘ L by the chain rule; otherwise both sides are 0. So D(F ∘ L)(y) = DF(L y) ∘ L always (ContinuousLinearEquiv.comp_right_fderiv).
- The same argument, applied inductively to iterated derivatives, gives iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (F ∘ L) y = (iteratedFDeriv ℝ k F (L y)) composed with L in every argument, for every k (ContinuousLinearEquiv.iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_right with the set univ, rewritten by iteratedFDerivWithin_univ).
- Likewise the translation w ↦ x + w is a diffeomorphism, so DT(w) = Dh(x + w) and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 T w = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h (x + w) for all w and every h (fderiv_comp_add_left, iteratedFDeriv_comp_add_left).

4. (First derivative.) By steps 2 and 3, DG(y)a = DT(L y)(L a) = Dh(x + (−s)y)((−s)a). By linearity of Dh(x − s y) this equals −s·Dh(x − s y)a.

5. (Second derivative.) By steps 2 and 3, D²G(y)(a, b) = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h (x + (−s)y) ![(−s)a, (−s)b]. A continuous multilinear map M in two variables satisfies M(c₁m₁, c₂m₂) = c₁c₂·M(m₁, m₂) (ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_smul_univ). So this equals (−s)(−s)·D²h(x − s y)(a, b) = s²·D²h(x − s y)(a, b). ∎

theorem Submission.dorag_ha_mv_affine_comp_deriv : ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (x : Euclid n) (s : ℝ) (y a b : Euclid n), fderiv ℝ (fun z : Euclid n => h (x - s • z)) y a = -(s * fderiv ℝ h (x - s • y) a) ∧ iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 (fun z : Euclid n => h (x - s • z)) y ![a, b] = s ^ 2 * iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h (x - s • y) ![a, b] := by
  intro n h x s y a b
  rcases eq_or_ne s 0 with rfl | hs
  · simp only [zero_smul, sub_zero, zero_mul, neg_zero]
    rw [iteratedFDeriv_const_of_ne (by norm_num)]
    simp
  · let L : Euclid n ≃L[ℝ] Euclid n := ContinuousLinearEquiv.smulLeft (Units.mk0 (-s) (neg_ne_zero.2 hs))
    have hL : ∀ z, L z = (-s) • z := fun z => rfl
    have hfun : (fun z : Euclid n => h (x - s • z)) = (fun w => h (x + w)) ∘ L := by
      funext z; simp [hL, sub_eq_add_neg, neg_smul]
    constructor
    · rw [hfun, ContinuousLinearEquiv.comp_right_fderiv, fderiv_comp_add_left]
      simp [hL, sub_eq_add_neg, neg_smul, map_smul]
    · rw [hfun]
      have := L.iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_right (fun w => h (x + w)) uniqueDiffOn_univ (mem_univ (L y)) 2
      rw [preimage_univ, iteratedFDerivWithin_univ, iteratedFDerivWithin_univ] at this
      rw [this, ContinuousMultilinearMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply, iteratedFDeriv_comp_add_left]
      have hv : (fun i : Fin 2 => (L : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid n) (![a, b] i)) = fun i => (-s) • ![a, b] i := by
        funext i; exact hL _
      rw [hv, ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_smul_univ]
      simp [hL, sub_eq_add_neg, neg_smul, sq]
proof_key_steps: If s = 0, G is constant, so both derivatives vanish, as do both right-hand sides.
If s ≠ 0, G = T ∘ L with L = (−s)·id a continuous linear equivalence and T = h(x + ·).
fderiv and iteratedFDeriv commute with composition by a continuous linear equivalence and with translation, for arbitrary functions (no differentiability needed).
Evaluate: DG(y)a = Dh(x − s y)((−s)a) = −s·Dh(x − s y)a, and by multilinearity D²G(y)(a, b) = (−s)²·D²h(x − s y)(a, b).

audit.reason: The exact affine identities hold for arbitrary h with the explicitly defined total derivatives. The proof handles s = 0 separately and uses unconditional translation and continuous-linear-equivalence composition formulas for s ≠ 0; multilinearity supplies s². No missing differentiability hypothesis or ordinary-chain-rule misuse occurs.
